correctness.rationale: For every nonzero pivot of a nonsingular 2×2 input the rank-one cross residual has sole nonzero magnitude |det A|/|a_ij|, giving Z=s1/|a_ij|. Exact squared-entry sampling yields E Z²=N s1²/(s1²+s2²)≤4. For b>2 the Gaussian regression identity gives E[X_i/X_j]=(b−2ρ²)/(b−2)≤b/(b−2), and Cauchy–Schwarz bounds every sketch-pivot probability by that factor times a_ij²/||A||F², proving E Z_b²≤4b/(b−2). On D_e, the independent χ²_b ratio implies exactly E Z_1²=1/e, E Z_2²=−2 log(e)/(1−e²), and limit 1+b/(b−2) for b≥3. For H_h symmetric SPD, row-exchange invariance makes sketch and exact pivot distributions identical; off-diagonal probability h²/(1+h²) yields exact E Z^p=(1+h)^p(1+h^(2−p))/(1+h²), diverging as h→0 for every p>2 even though κ≤2. The strict tail envelope follows by maximizing increasing off-pivot probability over h<1/(T−1). Independently checked several rational h moment identities and b=2 integral expressions.

originality.rationale: The primary Gaussian-sketch LU article establishes sufficient b≥3 pivot-probability domination, not necessity of b≥3 under the exact two-by-two mean-square normalization. The diagonal chi-square-ratio formulas at b=1,2 and the uniformly-conditioned higher-moment/tail obstruction are distinct further conclusions. Earlier squared-entry RPLU analyses give the baseline but not the sharp moment threshold and explicit counterexample laws.

Bound is first exact two-by-two pivot only, not multi-iteration or finite-precision behavior.
